topic: Agentic AI: hello world to enterprise
audience: Developers who can write a little Python and call a web API; no machine-learning background assumed. The course uses the Python 3.12 standard library and the official SDKs.
outcome: Build an agent that calls tools safely, grounds its answers in documents, remembers the right things, runs as a service and survives failures; know the enterprise practice (evals in CI, tracing, security, durable runs, tenancy, cost, governance) well enough to build it, operate it and pass a developer interview.

running_example.name: Brightside Outfitters support desk
running_example.why: Everyone has chased a late parcel, so the support desk needs no explanation; refunds make approval, idempotency and injection real problems.
running_example.evolution: order lookup agent (chapter 1) -> RAG, memory and a refund approval in a LangGraph graph (chapters 3-4) -> multi-agent with evals in CI, traces and security (chapter 5) -> reliable, cheap, served and durable with tenants (chapter 6)

llm.why: the course is about agents built on models; every model call is recorded once with a key and replayed without one

parts.title: Foundations: the first model call and the tool loop

lessons.title: Why agentic AI, and what an agent is (and is not)
lessons.goal: Tell an agent from a chatbot and from a fixed workflow, and say when not to build an agent.
concepts: Agent definition: model + tools + instructions in a loop
Degrees of autonomy and when not to build an agent
lessons.note: accepted after 1 fix round; recorded on gemini-3.1-flash-lite

lessons.title: Your first model call: messages, usage, cost and streaming
lessons.goal: Make a model call with the official SDK, read the usage and cost, and stream the answer.
concepts: Messages format, roles, chat templates; stateless API, client resends history
Streaming, rate limits, 429/503 handling, retries with backoff and jitter, timeouts

lessons.title: Tokens, context windows and sampling dials
lessons.goal: Count tokens, price a call, and see what the context window and the sampling controls do (and which models lock them).
concepts: Tokens, context window limits, token counting, price per million tokens
Sampling controls; reasoning/thinking effort dials; model choice small vs large
Fine-tuning vs distillation; fine-tuning for function calling

lessons.title: Prompting for agents and structured output with Pydantic
lessons.goal: Write a system prompt for an agent and get validated JSON back from the model, with a retry when it is invalid.
concepts: Structured output (JSON schema + Pydantic) and validation retries
Prompt engineering for agents: system prompts, examples, XML structure

lessons.title: The tool-call round trip on three vendor wire formats
lessons.goal: Declare a tool, let the model ask for it, run it and return the result, in the Claude, OpenAI and Gemini formats.
concepts: Tool/function calling round trip; schemas; tool_choice; parallel tool calls
under_the_hood: Tool/function calling round trip; schemas; tool_choice; parallel tool calls

parts.title: Core: an agent you can test and secure

lessons.title: Build the agent loop yourself, with step and cost caps
lessons.goal: Write the thought-action-observation loop with a step cap, a spend cap and repeated-call detection.
concepts: The agent loop: thought-action-observation (ReAct); implement it yourself with step and cost caps
Stopping conditions and loop detection (step cap, spend cap, repeated-call detection)
under_the_hood: AREA Tool calling and the agent loop (function schemas, tool round trip, stop conditions, tool errors)
The agent loop: thought-action-observation (ReAct); implement it yourself with step and cost caps
Stopping conditions and loop detection (step cap, spend cap, repeated-call detection)

lessons.title: Writing good tools: names, schemas and errors the model can act on
lessons.goal: Turn Python functions into tools the model uses correctly, and make tool errors something the model can recover from.
concepts: Python functions as tools; writing good tools (names, descriptions, narrow inputs, actionable errors)

lessons.title: Your first eval: a golden set and a test that needs no model
lessons.goal: Write the first 10 of the 30 golden tasks, with expected end states, and a pytest that scores a scripted fake agent.
concepts: Golden dataset, task success rate, pass@k, outcome vs trajectory grading
under_the_hood: Golden dataset, task success rate, pass@k, outcome vs trajectory grading

lessons.title: Safety basics: untrusted tool output, least privilege and approval for writes
lessons.goal: Show how a ticket can hijack an agent, then limit what each tool can do and flag every write for approval (the gate itself is lesson 14).
concepts: Prompt injection direct and indirect; lethal trifecta; layered mitigations; injection test set
Least privilege tools, read vs write, sandboxing, preventing destructive actions

lessons.title: Checkpoint: the order-lookup assistant (app v1)
lessons.goal: Ship a Basic-level agent with tools, caps, a golden set and safety checks, and run it with one command.

lessons.title: Why workflows come before autonomy: chaining, routing and parallel calls
lessons.goal: Compare a fixed pipeline with an agent on cost, reliability and debuggability, then build the three basic workflow shapes.
concepts: Task decomposition and prompt chaining with gates
under_the_hood: AREA Agentic design patterns and workflows (chaining, routing, parallel, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer, ReAct, plan-and-execute, reflection)

lessons.title: Orchestrator-workers and evaluator-optimizer loops
lessons.goal: Split one task across worker calls with an orchestrator, and add a judge that sends work back for a second pass.
concepts: Orchestrator-workers and evaluator-optimizer loops

lessons.title: ReAct, plan-and-execute and reflection: which fits and what each costs
lessons.goal: Choose a control pattern for a task from its cost, latency and failure modes, and see why reflection is used sparingly.
concepts: Planning: create and execute plans (plan-and-execute, ReWOO); planning with code execution
Reflection: self-critique, external feedback, measuring impact

lessons.title: A human approval gate with interrupt and resume
lessons.goal: Pause a refund before it is paid, wait for a person, and resume the same run safely.
concepts: Human-in-the-loop: approval gates, interrupt and resume, escalation
under_the_hood: Human-in-the-loop: approval gates, interrupt and resume, escalation

lessons.title: Short-term memory and context engineering: trim, summarise, compact, cache
lessons.goal: Keep a long conversation inside the window: trim, summarise and compact, and cache the stable prefix.
concepts: Short-term memory: message list, trimming, summarising, compaction
Context engineering: what goes in the window, just-in-time retrieval, tool-result clearing
Prompt caching and context caching

lessons.title: Long-term memory in SQLite: what to remember, forgetting and privacy
lessons.goal: Store customer facts the agent can recall later, with deletion and a rule for what must never be stored.
concepts: Long-term memory: semantic, episodic, procedural; hot-path vs background writes; forgetting and privacy

lessons.title: RAG basics: embeddings, chunking and cosine top-k

concepts: Embeddings, cosine similarity + top-k retrieval (implement from scratch)
